external_entities.name: duty engineer
external_entities.description: Sits on the corporate network and dispatches field crews from the console.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network. They open the dispatch console in their browser.

external_entities.name: scheduling partner
external_entities.description: Another company that publishes tomorrow's planned work as a SOAP feed.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company, publishes tomorrow's planned work.

processes.name: dispatch console
processes.description: Single-page JavaScript app the engineer opens in a browser; the corporate web host serves it, and it calls the dispatch API from a different origin.
processes.source_excerpt: The console is a single-page JavaScript app and our corporate web host serves it.
processes.technology: single-page JavaScript app in the browser

processes.name: dispatch API
processes.description: Runs in the production control plane; moves crews, changes a depot's work for the day, and reads and writes the dispatch database.
processes.source_excerpt: The console calls the dispatch API. The dispatch API runs in the production control plane.

processes.name: schedule importer
processes.description: Runs on the corporate network; every hour it pulls the partner's feed, parses it, archives the document, and posts the parsed work orders to the dispatch API.
processes.source_excerpt: Every hour it pulls the partner's SOAP feed over HTTPS and parses the XML document it gets back.
processes.technology: parses the partner's SOAP feed as an XML document; no product named

data_stores.name: dispatch database
data_stores.description: Holds the job orders, the crew names and the crew mobile numbers. Each job order carries the token or session that created it and nothing about the person behind it.
data_stores.source_excerpt: That database holds the job orders, the crew names and the crew mobile numbers.
data_stores.notes: The source states the at-rest protection is not written down anywhere, so this is a gap somebody registered rather than a topic nobody raised.

data_stores.name: schedule archive
data_stores.description: Folder on the corporate file store holding every XML document the importer downloads.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive, a folder on the corporate file store.
data_stores.technology: folder on the corporate file store

data_flows.name: open console
data_flows.description: The engineer opens the console in their browser and signs in to it.
data_flows.source_excerpt: They open the dispatch console in their browser.
data_flows.notes: The source states nobody wrote down how an engineer signs in.

data_flows.name: dispatch requests
data_flows.description: The console calls the dispatch API cross-origin, because the two are served from different origins; which origins the API allows, and whether it allows credentials, is not recorded.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console and the API are served from different origins, so the API answers the console cross-origin.
data_flows.data_description: dispatch actions: moving a crew and changing a depot's work for the day

data_flows.name: live job status
data_flows.description: The console opens a WebSocket to the dispatch API and holds it open for live job status.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console also opens a WebSocket to the dispatch API and holds it open for live job status.
data_flows.data_description: live job status for the crews on screen
data_flows.notes: The source states nobody wrote down whether the socket runs over TLS, whether its handshake is authenticated, or whether it checks the session again once open.

data_flows.name: pull schedule feed
data_flows.description: The importer pulls the partner's SOAP feed every hour and parses the XML document it gets back.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every hour it pulls the partner's SOAP feed over HTTPS and parses the XML document it gets back.
data_flows.data_description: tomorrow's planned work, as an XML document
data_flows.notes: The source states nothing was written down about how the partner identifies our importer, or how our importer identifies the partner.

data_flows.name: store schedule documents
data_flows.description: The importer writes each downloaded XML document into the archive folder.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive, a folder on the corporate file store.

data_flows.name: post work orders
data_flows.description: The importer posts the parsed work orders to the same dispatch API the console calls.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The importer then posts the parsed work orders to the same dispatch API the console calls. It presents an API token.
data_flows.authentication: an API token issued when the importer was built and never rotated since
data_flows.data_description: the work orders parsed out of the partner's feed

data_flows.name: read write job orders
data_flows.description: The API reads and writes the job orders and the crew details behind them.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
data_flows.data_description: job orders, crew names and crew mobile numbers

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: Where the duty engineers, their browsers and the schedule importer sit. Same company as the control plane, and a laptop here holds none of the control plane's rights.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: production control plane
trust_boundaries.description: Same company and same staff as the corporate network, and it holds the live estate: an account here can move a crew and change a depot's work for the day. Not reachable from the internet.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The control plane is the same company and the same staff, but it is the zone that holds the live estate: an account there can move a crew, and it can change the work a depot does that day. A corporate laptop holds none of those rights.

trust_boundaries.name: scheduling partner platform
trust_boundaries.description: Run by another company; the source says nothing else about it.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company, publishes tomorrow's planned work.

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch API is not reachable from the internet.
assumptions.basis: The source states the control plane is not reachable from the internet, and places the dispatch API in it; the source states nothing about the API's own exposure.
